newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rebels attack army-held northern town.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rebels attack army-held northern town.

text.p: Separatist Tamil Tiger guerrillas launched a pre-dawn attack on a key government-held northern town in the year's first major attack by rebels, military officials said on Thursday.
The attack, on the northern junction town of Paranthan on the mainland just south of the Jaffna peninsula, was continuing well into the morning, they said.
"The attack is still going on," a government military spokesman in Colombo told Reuters, adding it was too early to give details.

A large number of Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas had penetrated the town's defences and bombarded its military positions with artillery and mortars, other military officials in the north and east said.
The military, backed by air force helicopter gunships, were counterattacking, they added.
"The situation is under control," one military official told Reuters.
Casualty figures were not immediately available.
The LTTE, which is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island, were not immediately available for comment.

Government forces captured Paranthan, (280 km) 185 miles north of the capital Colombo, from the rebels last July. The town is on a major road junction just south of the government-controlled northern Jaffna peninsula.
Paranthan sits astride the main north-south highway from Colombo to Jaffna and controls the road junction connecting to the rebel-held northeastern town of Mullaitivu.
Last July government forces pushed further into rebel territory shortly after capturing Paranthan, and in August took control of Kilinochchi, the last major town controlled by the rebels.

Paranthan is the first military base to be attacked by the rebels this year. The rebels in early December overran a police commando camp at Pulukunawa in the eastern Amparai district, killing 36 security personnel.

Earlier this week, the rebels said they killed at least eight soldiers in a separate attack on Tuesday night on the army's northern forward defences in Vavuniya district, 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Colombo.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
